newMemories.name: limit-function-type-contract.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit limitFunction requires a PromiseLike return; its result exposes only the call signature plus clearQueue
type: project
---
In the p-limit project, index.d.ts declares the exported limitFunction as `limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>, options: Options): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>`. This is a type-level contract grounded in the declarations, not a proven runtime restriction. The input function must return a PromiseLike (distinct from Promise); the tsd assertion `expectError(limitFunction((_a: string) => 'x', {concurrency: 1}))` in index.test-d.ts records that a bare sync-returning function is a type error. The options parameter is required and typed Options, whose concurrency is mandatory and rejectOnClear an optional boolean. The return type is a callable yielding Promise<ReturnType> intersected with only clearQueue from LimitFunction, so activeCount, pendingCount, concurrency and map are not reachable on the limited function; this matches expectType<Promise<string>>(lf('input')) and expectType<void>(lf.clearQueue()). By contrast the default export's LimitFunction call signature accepts `(...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType`, which does allow non-Promise returns.

<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(
		function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType> | ReturnType,
		...arguments_: Arguments
	): Promise<ReturnType>;

newMemories.name: p-limit-concurrency-reservation.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit reserves a concurrency slot at enqueue time before actual task invocation
type: project
---
In the p-limit project's index.js, the concurrency slot is reserved before the task starts: enqueue() always pushes the queue item and calls resumeNext() only when activeCount < concurrency, and resumeNext() re-checks `activeCount < concurrency && queue.size > 0`, increments activeCount, and dequeues and runs exactly one item. The wrapped function is not invoked synchronously with the limit(...) call; enqueue wraps the queue push in a new Promise and chains `.then(run.bind(...))`, so invocation happens in a later microtask. run() calls resolve(result) as soon as the task promise exists — the caller's promise adopts the task promise's eventual state without the caller having awaited completion — while activeCount stays incremented until `await result` finishes inside the try/catch whose empty catch only suppresses internal unhandled rejections and preserves the original rejection for the caller. The slot is released by next(): activeCount-- followed by resumeNext(), so one freed slot immediately admits one waiter.

newMemories.name: p-limit-clearqueue-semantics.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit clearQueue drops pending promises unsettled by default; with rejectOnClear they reject with AbortError
type: project
---
In the p-limit project, clearQueue() affects only queued, not-yet-started items and does not cancel promises that are already running (stated in the index.d.ts doc comment). Without rejectOnClear (default false) it calls queue.clear() and returns, so the discarded items' captured reject handlers are never invoked and those pending promises are not settled by clearQueue; the test.js 'clearQueue' test only asserts pendingCount going from 3 to 0 without awaiting the dropped promises. With rejectOnClear: true it dequeues each remaining item and rejects it with a single shared reason taken from `AbortSignal.abort().reason`; the pnpm test run on Node v22.23.2 reported '✔ clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled', whose assertions expect name 'AbortError'. Note test.js gates the rejectOnClear tests with `process.versions.node.startsWith('20.') ? test.skip : test`, so on Node 20 those assertions are skipped rather than verified. Independently of the type-level option, index.js enforces rejectOnClear at runtime construction time: a non-boolean throws TypeError('Expected `rejectOnClear` to be a boolean').

evidence.quote:
Discard pending promises that are waiting to run.

	This might be useful if you want to tear down the queue at the end of your program's lifecycle or discard any function calls referencing an intermediary state of your app.

	Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running.

	When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`.
	This is recommended if you await the returned promises, for example with `Promise.all`, so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.
✔ clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled (109ms)

newMemories.name: p-limit-nested-deadlock-warning.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit warns that calling the same limit inside its own limited task can deadlock; use a separate limiter
type: project
---
The p-limit project's index.d.ts call-signature documentation for the LimitFunction states: "Warning: Avoid calling the same `limit` function inside a function that is already limited by it. This can create a deadlock where inner tasks never run. Use a separate limiter for inner tasks." This is the documented source-level restriction as declared in the project; it should guide future maintenance of code that nests limiter calls.

evidence.quote: Warning: Avoid calling the same `limit` function inside a function that is already limited by it. This can create a deadlock where inner tasks never run. Use a separate limiter for inner tasks.
